AFDSTO

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Sacramento CA
1255 PM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

For additional details on weather and expected impacts over the
next 7 days, please visit weather.gov/sto/briefing.

.KEY MESSAGES... 

 - Cold morning lows and Valley/Delta fog Saturday morning. 
  
 - Weaker storm system over the weekend, with minor snow
   accumulations and light rainfall. 

 - Briefly dry conditions on Monday before active weather returns
   for the days leading up to and including Thanksgiving. This
   storm is not anticipated to be as wet or snowy as the most
   recent system. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

...Today - Saturday AM...

RADAR currently shows a few showers continuing to linger over the
Sierra this afternoon, though any remaining impacts from this
precipitation will be limited. Drier conditions prevail the rest
of the day and into early Saturday. With the passage of this
latest system, interior NorCal will see cold morning lows early 
Saturday, with temperatures in the 30s across the Valley and teens
to 20s in the mountains. Areas of frost and patchy Valley fog are
also anticipated. Remember to drive carefully through any fog and
allow for extra travel time tomorrow morning.

...The Weekend - Next Week...

A weak system moves across the area late Saturday morning into
Sunday, bringing light Valley rain and mountain snow above 4000 
feet. Latest forecast from WPC indicates precipitation amounts 
around 0.10 inches or less across the majority of the Valley (up
to 0.25 inches in the northern Sacramento Valley), and 0.25 to 
around 0.40 inches over the mountains. Forecasted snow amounts 2 
to 5 inches above 4000 feet, and a few flurries down to around 
3500 feet. 

After a break Monday, a stronger system is expected to arrive 
mid-next week bringing another around of Valley rain and mountain 
snow. Ensembles continue to show uncertainty with this upcoming 
system, but while we will be seeing periods of rain, mountain
snow, and gusty winds, confidence is good that this system will
have lower precipitation totals and weaker winds than the most
recent storm. Currently the chance for an inch or more of rain is
50-70% in the Sacramento Valley and 25-40% in the northern San 
Joaquin Valley. Probabilities for snow have trended down slightly
from yesterday, with limited potential for snow totals reaching 8
inches, and the chance for totals of 6 inches or greater around 
50-75% within the Sierra and southern Cascades. Be sure to stay up
to date with the latest forecast information as we head into 
Thanksgiving week.

&&

.AVIATION...

VFR/MVFR conditions are forecast to prevail this afternoon as
ceilings improve and/or skies clear with a departing storm system.
Potential for patchy fog will develop overnight, particularly 
from the Sacramento area terminals and locations south heading
into the San Joaquin Valley. Winds will generally be less than 12
kt through the 24 hour TAF period.

&&

.STO WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
